data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Limits Tanker Transit Through the Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
The United States has required tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz to sail only during specific time windows in order to receive military protection. According to Sina Finance, the move comes after Washington stepped up attacks on vessels sailing at night.

Since May, Washington has provided air cover for ships taking the route along the Omani coast on the southern side of the strait to deter Iranian attacks and help ensure some oil can be exported out of the Gulf. Shipowners must apply through the U.S. Naval Coordination Center for Shipping and Naval Cooperation and Guidance, known as NCAGS, which then gives crews navigation coordinates and allows vessels to pass during broad nighttime windows under U.S. fighter protection.

Emails seen by the media showed that in early September, those transit windows were narrowed to two specific daily periods, with affected ships told to depart at designated times such as 9 a.m. One email said the center was currently providing dynamically adjusted recommended transit windows each day, while another said night transit was not the safest time of day for commercial shipping.

The U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. military operations in the Middle East, said the NCAGS emails spoke for themselves. Since the U.S. and Israel struck Iran in February, Iranian forces have attacked dozens of ships trying to pass through the disputed waterway. As both sides have intensified pressure on commercial shipping, the U.S. has shifted escort protection to fixed day and night periods.

data.title: ECB Governing Council Member Kocher Warns High Oil Prices Could Force More Rate Hikes
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher warned that if oil prices continue to hover around $100 a barrel before year-end, the central bank will have to raise interest rates further. After the European Central Bank raised borrowing costs for the second time on Thursday, the Austrian central bank governor said inflation risks were higher than a few months ago because tensions in the Middle East remained elevated and energy prices stayed high. Since the collapse of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement in early July, oil prices have risen more than 45% and moved above $100 a barrel, while European natural gas prices have nearly doubled since June to close to 80 euros per megawatt hour. Kocher said that if oil and gas prices move toward an adverse scenario, monetary policy must take those changes into account, and he added that inflation risks would intensify further.

data.title: CATL Launches Record A-Share Buyback Plan, Starts First 200 Billion Yuan Repurchase
data.description:
CATL said on September 11 that it bought back 604,300 A-share shares through a centralized bidding process on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange for about 200 million yuan, marking the first execution of its 200 billion yuan to 400 billion yuan repurchase plan, according to Jiemian News. The company said the shares will be cancelled and the registered capital reduced, with the buyback funded by its own or self-raised cash and carried out within 12 months after shareholder approval.

The 400 billion yuan ceiling is the largest single buyback amount ever announced in the A-share market. CATL said the first repurchase was done at 330.15 yuan to 331.61 yuan per share, below the plan's 573 yuan-per-share cap. The company also said the move reflects confidence in its long-term outlook amid stock-price volatility and concerns about valuation, while its earlier buybacks were mainly used for equity incentives or employee shareholding plans.

CATL's shares closed at 330.51 yuan on September 11, down nearly 30% from this year's intraday high of 468.75 yuan in May. Jiemian News reported that investors are watching whether automakers accelerate efforts to reduce reliance on CATL, after Li Auto said on September 7 that all of its models would use self-developed batteries and Xiaomi Auto named CALB and Sunwoda Power as strategic battery partners. Despite the share-price decline, CATL reported first-half revenue of 276.917 billion yuan, up 54.8%, and net profit of 43.284 billion yuan, up 41.98%.

data.title: U.S. Authorities Probe Polymarket Bets Tied to KPMG-Audited Earnings
data.description:
A cluster of 19 linked Polymarket accounts placed concentrated bets over the past few months on earnings reports from publicly listed companies audited by KPMG, including Wells Fargo, Home Depot, DoorDash, and General Mills. According to Odaily, the accounts made 42 trades, won 41 of them, and generated about $22,000 in profit.

Funds reportedly moved among the 19 accounts, suggesting they may have been controlled by the same person or team. U.S. law enforcement is investigating a KPMG employee suspected of using Polymarket for insider trading after betting on whether quarterly results at listed companies would beat market expectations. It is not yet clear whether the account cluster is linked to the employee, and the analysis does not by itself prove insider trading. KPMG said it has a zero-tolerance policy toward trading on nonpublic client information and has strengthened related monitoring.

data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI Codex Fixes Astra Quality Issues, Plans Reset Before Midnight
data.description: According to Jin10, OpenAI Codex product lead Tibo said the team has identified and fixed multiple defects in Astra and will carry out a reset before local midnight today, which is noon Beijing time. Tibo said the team confirmed and fixed several issues after working with some users, including abnormal triggering of skills written for earlier models, an optional context-management experiment that could cause early stopping or replies to old messages and has now been disabled, and misconfigured engines that have been removed after causing measurable quality declines in tail traffic. The team also made smaller improvements and said the overall experience should improve noticeably, including more consistent execution, better tracking of users' latest messages, and more thorough checks of results as work progresses.

data.title: STOCKS | Trump Surgeon General Pick Holds Stakes in Tobacco and Beverage Stocks
data.description:
Financial disclosure documents released on Thursday showed that Nicole Saphier, U.S. President Donald Trump's nominee for Surgeon General, holds investments in Philip Morris International, as well as beverage companies including Monster Beverage, Coca-Cola, and PepsiCo. According to Sina Finance, she disclosed the holdings in an ethics agreement and said she would divest all or part of the positions, while also selling shares in several major pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, including Eli Lilly, Biogen, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, Merck, and AbbVie.

U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has made cracking down on unhealthy ultra-processed foods a work priority. According to Sina Finance, Saphier also supports removing food additives, reducing ultra-processed foods in the diet, and encouraging exercise.

Saphier is the founder of DropRx, which sells “physician-formulated” herbal dietary supplements. According to Sina Finance, she also serves as breast imaging director at the Monmouth branch of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New Jersey and was previously a Fox News commentator.

The Surgeon General is known as America’s top doctor and is responsible for delivering authoritative scientific information to the public and guiding healthier behavior. According to Sina Finance, Saphier's Senate confirmation hearing is scheduled for September 16 (Wednesday).

data.title: STOCKS | Huatai Securities Says U.S. CPI Beat Makes a September Rate Hike a Must
data.description: According to Jin10, Huatai Securities said August core inflation rose more than expected on a month-on-month basis, making a September Federal Reserve rate hike a "must" and increasing the credibility risk of not hiking in September. The report said August nonfarm payrolls also beat expectations, Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $100, and August CPI became the key variable in market pricing of whether the Fed will hike in September. It added that core inflation in August accelerated more than expected, while the core services ex-housing component watched by the Fed did not show further signs of slowing. The report also said low inventories, concerns over surging oil prices, AI-driven price increases passing through to downstream sectors, and a new round of local tariffs could all disrupt the pace of U.S. disinflation. Looking ahead, the report said CPI data may push neutral voter Christopher Waller to turn hawkish at the September FOMC meeting, reducing internal Fed resistance to a September hike. It added that August data also cleared obstacles for a rate hike, and if Kevin Warsh fails to deliver on his hawkish pledge from the August Jackson Hole meeting in September, the Fed's credibility will face a greater challenge and long-term U.S. Treasury yields will be harder to control.

data.title: Larry Ellison Enters Trading Plan To Sell Up To $7.5 Billion Of Oracle Stock
data.description: According to CNBC, Oracle founder Larry Ellison has entered into a trading plan that would allow him to sell up to 50 million shares of the software company, worth about $7.5 billion at current prices. Ellison adopted the plan on June 22, and it is set to end on Oct. 24, according to a regulatory filing published Friday. He controls more than 40% of Oracle, according to FactSet, and would still own 1.1 billion shares if he sells all of the stock covered by the plan. Since the start of this century, Ellison has never sold more than 25,000 Oracle shares at any one time, according to FactSet. Oracle said in its earnings report on Thursday that it beat estimates and posted 121% year-over-year growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

data.title: Hormuz Strait Ship Traffic Falls to Seven After Saudi Pipeline Attack

According to ChainCatcher, Iraq confirmed that the drone attack on Saudi Arabia originated from within its territory, and Saudi Arabia has agreed not to take retaliatory action for now at Iraq's request.
